No, I would probably not change my career plan a year before my graduation simply because I felt unhappy. If I did feel this way in my studies, I would not have chosen it in the first place, or I would have found it out much earlier. At this stage, I should have finished learning most of the core courses of this major, and tested the waters with some internship experiences. If I gave up on the career path, all the efforts I'd made previously would go down the drain. In addition, it would be reckless to decide that I would be unhappy in this career even before I had seriously devoted myself to it. In fact, not many people can pursue a career that they really have passion for from the outset. Many people actually come to love their careers after they have put in considerable time and energy. Even if I did feel unhappy, a more rational choice would be to finish my undergraduate study first, and consider changing my field of study at the postgraduate stage.

In addition, I've been preparing to take the tests for the psychological consultant certificate.

许多人认为，他们的职业道路始于找到工作之时。但其实，它始于童年时期。孩子们最早期的经历可能会对其未来的职业选择产生影响。例如，童年早期去医院看病和去学校上学的经历会让许多年轻人选择从事医疗或教育行业。但这样的选择有时候会与父母的意愿产生矛盾：父母总希望按照自己的身份或自己年轻时想成为的样子培养孩子从事合意的职业。

在职业规划中，父母在年轻人成功确定自己想要一心投入的职业方面起着重要作用。父母能采取的最好办法不是将自己的意愿强加于孩子，而是支持他们的热情。支持孩子的途径包括帮助其阅读他们感兴趣的领域的材料，让他们接触这个行业，提供信息让他们了解想要实现的职业目标可能带来的好处，以及他们可能要做出的牺牲。

The author thinks that freediving can be an effective tool for marine research. In the last three paragraphs, he first examines the disadvantages of scuba diving as opposed to freediving by quoting one freediving researcher as saying, "You're not only removed from the environment, you're disrupting it." He then moves on to quote another researcher on the importance of having intimate contact with the animals. Finally he explicitly expresses his attitude by saying "surely we should."

Hal Whitehead holds a negative attitude toward the use of freediving in marine research based on his own research experience. In the early years of studying sperm whales, he and his team swam with the whales but they "got virtually no useful scientific information and it disturbed the whales." So he thinks the use of freediving in the DareWin project is problematic "both scientifically and ethically."

I think freediving is a proper tool for marine research. Freediving has a minimal impact on marine life. Unlike noisy scuba or remotely operated vehicles, the freediving approach doesn't scare off the animals. Researchers don't have to rely on heavy equipment. They can enter the water quietly and do not leave a trail of bubbles. In this way, they can get close enough to the animals to observe their undisturbed natural behavior. This natural and unobtrusive approach can offer us a rare glimpse into the marine world.

I am Li Hua. I was born in a city called Cixi in Zhejiang Province. I did not know anything about Yan dialect until last summer when I paid a visit to a distant uncle of mine at Guanhaiwei, a small town about half-an-hour's drive away from my home. My uncle told me that in the northwestern part of the town, some elderly people speak a dialect called "Yan," which is completely unintelligible to outsiders, even to the people living in other parts of the town. Local legend has it that Yu Qiaqing, a tycoon born in Zhejiang, used Yan dialect as a secret code for communication in the old Shanghai stock exchange market in the early 20th century. The dialect was also used by local guerrillas to transmit secret information in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression.

How Yan dialect came into being has remained a mystery. Some people believe that the dialect was closely related to the immigrants from Fujian Province during the construction of the military establishment at Guanhaiwei over 600 years ago. Another hypothesis is that the dialect was brought by the garrison led by Qi Jiguang, a military general in the Ming Dynasty, in their defense against Japanese pirates along the coastal regions of Zhejiang Province.

I was immediately intrigued by Yan dialect during my visit, and I wanted to learn more about it. For example, what is a more plausible explanation for the origin of Yan dialect? Why didn't Yan dialect merge into the more dominant local dialect of the town? What can we do to preserve the dialect when only a few people at Guanhaiwei can now speak it?

In order to answer these questions, I will need to read published papers and local chronicles, interview local people, and examine the sound patterns of the dialect. I hope that by exploring the origin of Yan dialect, I will be better able to understand the history and culture of my hometown.

The submersible could carry three researchers in each deep-diving operation. Once the submersible begins formal operation, excluding the time for the ascent and descent, it will enable researchers to carry out around six hours of scientific tasks at the depths of the ocean.

Now I'm standing here with my camera on, while the explorers are preparing for their descent into the Greenland ice sheet by drilling deep into the ice. They create two intersecting holes into the bed of a now frozen-over ice river, running a rope through them in the shape of a V to anchor their lines. It would be more than strong enough to carry their weight, but they drill a second anchor as well, just in case. Then Matt, a cave explorer who has spent more than a year of his life beneath the ground, gets ready. He begins to lower himself into the cave. Even from where I stand, I can hear running water somewhere. The hole, one of the explorers believes, ultimately penetrates more than 500 meters into the ice. Matt is dangling from the wall of this deep hole. When I hear ice breaking and falling, it brings my heart up into my throat. Exploration in the ice cave is risky, but explorers are willing to take the risk in order to study the movement of water deep underground and then better understand the effects of climate change on the melting ice.

I would tell Sister Mary Jucunda that exploring space is not cheap but the benefits for humankind are enormous. Economic, scientific and technological returns of space exploration have far exceeded the investment. A lot of space technology has military and commercial applications. For example, satellite technology forms the backbone of the GPS systems that we all use to navigate. The central air-conditioning system on Beijing subway Line 9 uses temperature control technology that was developed for the Chang'e-3 lunar probe. But it's not just about technology that benefits our daily lives. Space exploration can serve as a stimulus for children to enter the field of science and engineering. It fuels curiosity, inspiration, and creativity. It inspires younger generations to devote their talent and passion to science.

In the long run, with all the new technological and scientific knowledge which we will apply to the improvement of life, space exploration will contribute tremendously to the relief and eventual solution of many grave problems we are facing here on Earth like hunger and poverty.

In this sentence, "rose," "collapsed," "redrew," "swerved" and "shimmied" are used metaphorically. "Rose," whose literal meaning is "increased in number, amount, or value," means "achieved power and success" in this sentence. "Collapsed," whose literal meaning is "broke into pieces and fell down," means "failed suddenly or became too weak to continue" in this sentence. "Redrew," whose literal meaning is "reproduced a picture using a pencil, pen, etc.," means "changed the borders of a country, region, etc." in this sentence. "Swerved," whose literal meaning is "made a sudden sideways movement while moving forward, usu. in order to avoid hitting sth.," means "had many bends and twists" in this sentence. "Shimmied," whose literal meaning is "moved forward or backward while also quickly moving slightly from side to side," means "had many bends and turns" in this sentence.
In this sentence, "felled" is used metaphorically. "Felled," whose literal meaning is "cut down a tree," means "knocked sb. down with great force" in this sentence.
In this sentence, "voyaging" is used metaphorically. "Voyaging," whose literal meaning is "traveling to a place, esp. by sea or in space," means "traveling over a long distance" in this sentence.

In this sentence, the word "catapulted" is used metaphorically. "Catapulted," whose literal meaning is "pushed or thrown very hard so that it moved through the air very quickly," means "caused to experience sth. suddenly and unexpectedly" in this sentence.

According to the passage, the potential implications of longevity for society are very complex, and are more negative than positive. Prolonged lifespans will probably worsen existing social and economic problems. Firstly, it may widen the gap between the rich and the poor if anti-aging treatment is expensive. Secondly, it is difficult to predict what kind of role a large proportion of older people will play in the workforce. Thirdly, we still don't know how society will cope with the needs for enormous pension pots, more education, more frequent job shifts, and longevity-related health problems that come with old age.

For individuals, however, the implications of a long life are quite positive. With a longer life, one would have more possibilities and new beginnings in life. As a result, one could change careers, take long breaks, go back to school again to learn something new, and enjoy life more. The negative side of a long life is the diseases that come with old age, especially cardiovascular and bone diseases, as well as dementia.

Besides what is mentioned in the passage, I think a world of longevity would have a radical effect on other aspects of society including medical care, family life, and natural resources. Firstly, longevity-related chronic illnesses would exert high pressure on the nation's social security system and medical care sector. Secondly, living longer means being able to spend more time with our loved ones. Lastly, natural resources like water and land might be in greater shortage.

I will definitely want to live an eternal life if given the chance. Firstly, I will have many more years to learn and grow. I will acquire a lot more knowledge. Then I could use my knowledge and creativity to help build a better society. Secondly, I could live with my loved ones for more years. Perhaps I could see my great-grandchildren growing up. Thirdly, I will have enough time to pursue my interests and live a wonderful life.

I have searched for information on dealing with an aging population. I think that we can prepare for an aging society in the following aspects:

Invest heavily in research on major old-age-related diseases and regenerative therapies. Lower the cost of medicines and medical care and make them affordable for low-income families. Develop health-care robots to assist elderly people in daily activities and lower the cost of daily care.

Develop a sound social security system to cover longevity-related expenses. Develop schemes which let old people or their families contribute a certain amount of money on a monthly basis to an account so that they can get a monthly income in retirement.

Develop more life-long learning programs to tap into old people's potential as well as to promote personal development and social integration. Encourage skilled elders to participate in interactions with the young. Develop more types of health-care plans that offer the elderly more choices, such as nursing homes, assisted-living, and home care.

Apart from a healthy body, the bond with the world and the desire to lead a productive and meaningful life are critical for the well-being of elderly people. Therefore, young people can help them in the following ways:

First, young people can learn from them, so that the elderly people could feel that they can offer something useful to other people. Being useful makes one fulfilled.

Second, we can help them get involved in some volunteer service. The interactions with the outside world bring them meaning and emotional satisfaction.

Third, we can expose them to the latest technology, especially electronic devices. We can teach them how to use the latest electronic devices such as cellphones and computers. This would help them connect with others across distance, get in touch with the world, and see the world from a new perspective.

In 1949, the average lifespan of Chinese people was less than 35 years. In 2018, the figure reached 77. The average lifespan more than doubled within 70 years. How did China achieve this? First and foremost, this was thanks to the improvement in people's physical fitness, a direct result of the improvement in people's diet and the optimization of their dietary structure. Meanwhile, rising levels of medical and health care also played a key role in extending people's lifespan. In the future, the physical fitness of the Chinese people will continue to be strengthened, their quality of life will be steadily improved, and their healthy lifespan will continue to be extended. This is the development goal of Healthy China.

The author introduces the issue of longevity by alternating between its benefits and potential risks. In Paras. 2-5, the author constructs a positive image of a future society where aging has been abolished. This is a future which everybody desires and which is likely to come true thanks to modern medical science and technology. To present another side of the issue, the author raises broad social and economic questions (Paras. 7-8): the cost of anti-aging treatment, the role and status of older employees, their tendency to be conservative, etc. In Paras. 9-10, the positive side is discussed again. Then in Paras. 11-12, the author returns to the potential risks and cautions against eternal life without eternal youth and health. In the end, the author concludes the passage on an optimistic note. In the passage, both the desirable effects and potential risks of the longevity issue are discussed in depth, and the argument is structured in a balanced way.

Expressions and structures which introduce an opinion or argument in the passage: that was thanks to; optimists claim; is known to; which suggests that; with the thought that; From an individual viewpoint; For society as a whole; since. Modals which strengthen an argument: must; should. Modals which weaken an argument: may; might; would.

Imagine a world in which doctors could remove or repair a defective gene in a human being, or replace it with a healthy copy. The development of gene-editing technology has opened up the possibility of directly modifying or removing the cause of genetic diseases. From an individual's viewpoint, this prospect is very desirable. For society as a whole, though, it will have profound effects.

Supporters of gene editing claim that this life-saving therapy provides great benefits. For example, research shows that by modifying T-cells, doctors can locate and kill cancer cells. Gene editing may extend the human lifespan and greatly improve the quality of life.

For its opponents, however, a lot of things must be taken into consideration if we do not want to risk its potentially negative consequences. The most immediate challenge will be the safety issue. Another concern is the ethical issue: People might resort to gene editing for genome enhancement rather than for medical purposes. Therefore, many countries ban or discourage research on germline editing because of ethical and safety concerns.

However, in spite of its potential benefits, scientists and medical workers generally agree that until gene editing is proved to be safe and ethical, it should not be used for clinical purposes.
The two things compared in the passage are hormones and text messaging.

The author's purpose in using this analogy is to compare the similarities between the two: Both are messages to prompt the recipient into action; both may be silent and ignored; and both are predictive and may make mistakes.

I think that the analogy is well drawn because the ways that hormones and text messages are sent are similar in many aspects. Text messaging is an everyday phenomenon of modern society, so its features are easy for us to understand. These features are picked out and used to describe hormones which are more intangible and hidden. Learning about the messages sent by hormones in terms of text messaging helps us to see things that we might not understand clearly if we stuck to medical explanation and medical terms for hormones. Therefore, this is a good analogy in that it illuminates a difficult and not commonly understood field with reference to an everyday phenomenon.

I do sometimes get messages from my body. One message is dry eyes. I spend a few hours every day looking at the electronic screens of my cell phone and my computer. The dry eyes make me realize that too much screen time impacts my vision and the health of my eyes. Another message that I get is hair loss. I used to pull my hair back tightly into a knot. I also used chemicals to dye or perm my hair very often. Then I noticed the hair loss, which made me realize that lost hair couldn't come back. Now I let my hair down naturally, and dye or perm my hair as little as possible.

Yes, I do. I experienced a prolonged period of stress in high school because of the heavy pressure of preparing for the college entrance examination. At that time, I constantly worried that I would fail the exam. The anxiety became so serious that I could not easily go to sleep at night and felt drowsy during the day. My memory deteriorated, and I was not able to focus. I didn't understand these physical and emotional messages from my body until I talked about my problem with my parents. The symptoms of anxiety gradually disappeared, and I finally got a satisfactory score in the college entrance exam.

Qipao, as a traditional and iconic costume in China, can well show the charm of females. Most of the early advocates of qipao were women who rebelled against feudal constraints and pursued gender equality. Today, qipao plays a very prominent role on diplomatic occasions in China. In the long course of Chinese history, designers have never stopped improving and innovating the design of qipao. On the one hand, designers look for aesthetic perception and draw inspiration from elaborate ancient Chinese artworks. On the other hand, they continually integrate current fashion elements into qipao design. They have also brought these masterpieces, which are collaborations of fashion and classical art, to the world stage.

This passage doesn't follow the typical structure of an issue analysis essay. Unlike other essays that normally present an opinion on an issue at the beginning of the essay, this passage presents its thesis statement in the conclusion part.

The status of fashion within the sphere of fine art has long been the subject of debate. Some designers identified themselves as artists, considering their work as art, while others regarded themselves simply as fashion designers, viewing fashion and art as two separate realms.

From one point of view, the main differences between fashion and art could be found in their utility and temporality. However, from another point of view, in the real art world, these distinctions have never been so clear-cut, and today they're increasingly being blurred. Even so, fashion is still not exactly art. They share more of a symbiotic relationship.

Though fashion and art are closely connected, the intrinsic difference between the two remains in terms of utility. "Art is art. Fashion is fashion. However, they can exist together."

There is no doubt that everyone needs clothes. But when choosing a garment, people of different ages and genders may have different opinions regarding this question, that is: What is more important, comfort or style? My viewpoint is that comfort is certainly more important than style.

Some may argue that the foremost thing for wearing clothes is to make yourself look more beautiful, pleasing and attractive, and comfort is secondary. But I hold the opposite view. What you think is "beautiful" may not be beautiful at all in others' eyes. I prefer to wear comfortable clothes, and I think the texture of the fabric is the most important. Clothes made of wool, cotton and silk are more comfortable than those made of some synthetic fibers.

In a sense, fashion is deceptive, and style is illusive. To buy comfortable clothes is something we can control, and wearing comfortable clothes benefits our mood and health.

From left to right, I think the first and third pictures are drawn by robots.

The structure of the first picture is not clear, because the locations of the trees, paths, and hills in the painting are rather chaotic. The color is monotonous, and the lines of the trunks and branches are relatively rigid. There is not a natural connection between the trunks and the leaves. It looks like a child's drawing.

As for the third picture, the outlines of the man in the painting are blurry. The man's facial expression is stiff and unnatural. The man's eyebrows are painted in a very rough manner, which lacks softness and fineness. The whole face lacks vitality. This painting also fails to reflect the brightness of the light.

I think that we may misinterpret other humans' artworks. Understanding other humans' artworks is no easy job. It involves many factors, such as the artwork itself, the knowledge about the creator of the artwork, and our own understanding. Artists often create artworks depending on their state of mind, mood, and social circumstances. We need to put ourselves in the artist's shoes and see things from his / her perspective. But this is not easy to do. Most people will just look at the artwork and make their own interpretation or come to their own conclusion. For example, "The Persistence of Memory" is a surrealist painting by Spanish painter Salvador Dalí. When I looked at it, I believed that the soft, egg-like pocket watches indicated that time was passing quickly. But later, I learned that the painter was inspired by the image of cheese melting in the sun. Apparently my interpretation was wrong.

To answer this question, we first need to define what machinic art is. My definition is that it has to be not only created by machines, but also conceived by machines of their own volition. It should not be based on any human idea, nor should it be intervened in by humans in any way. The "Portrait of Edmond de Belamy" is the first AI art in the world made by an algorithm to be sold by an auction house. It is not a product of a human mind, but the cumulative result of machine learning. So, I would say it's a piece of real machinic art.

I think it is reasonable for the machinic art being auctioned at such a high price. The "Portrait of Edmond de Belamy" depicts a man in black coat with a white collar. I guess the buyer may be intrigued by the idea that this artwork was created by a machine, and he / she may fancy that someday its value will increase, or that high technology does deserve this high price. Perhaps it is not the painting itself that is highly valued, but the fact that machines or algorithms can do the painting job.

Yes, I agree that humans are not able to understand machinic art. We humans are even not able to understand other humans' work, not to mention the work of the machines supposing there is real machinic work. To understand an artistic work, we need empathy. We need to use our own conscious experience to ask what could possibly motivate us to make such an artwork ourselves. But we humans cannot understand what machines are thinking while they create artworks, because we have no idea of their perspective, and we do not know their purpose of making certain artworks.

The theme of the passage is women's longing for freedom in a society where they feel inferior or low in status. From Louise's reaction to the sad news of her husband's death, we can see that she has been feeling powerless in their relationship, with her husband often imposing his will upon her. Now that her husband has gone, she feels she could enjoy the freedom without him and live for herself. Louise's death isn't caused by her sudden realization that her husband's death has granted her autonomy or by her joy at seeing her husband's safe return. She dies of her broken dream—the sudden loss of freedom and autonomy which she has been dreaming of.

In her room, Mrs. Mallard "could see in the open square before her house the tops of trees that were all aquiver with the new spring life." Her heart, too, is all aquiver with the hope of a new life.

"There were patches of blue sky showing here and there through the clouds that had met and piled one above the other in the west facing her window." Blue sky is showing though it was previously covered. Previously, Mrs. Mallard longed for her life to end, seeing nothing but restrictions. Now her life seems full of hope.

After hearing the news of her husband's death, Mrs. Mallard goes away to her room. "There stood, facing the open window, a comfortable, roomy armchair." The armchair symbolizes rest from her oppressive life and freedom from societal expectations.

Josephine is worried that Mrs. Mallard has locked herself in her room and is making herself ill. Mrs. Mallard is actually in the room thinking about how wonderful her life is going to be. That is both situational and dramatic irony.

Mrs. Mallard dies from the shock of seeing her husband coming back. The doctors say she dies of "the joy that kills." We know Mrs. Mallard is nowhere near full of joy. That's dramatic irony.

Bi Feiyu is a renowned contemporary Chinese writer, currently serving as chairman of Jiangsu Writers Association. He has won many prizes for his works, including Mao Dun Literature Prize and Lu Xun Literature Prize. He attaches great importance to the historical process of contemporary China and stylistic experimentation, exploring the language, rhythm, and form of novels in various aspects. He sets very high standards for the language of his novels and develops a unique and highly recognizable style of his own. With the goal of achieving wisdom and originality, he has made every effort to avoid clichés in his writing. Drawing on his experience of poetry writing in his early years, his novels are often colored with poetic imagery, leaving people a lingering impression.

The book that I've recently finished reading is Wuthering Heights by Emily Brontë, one of my favorite English novelists and poets. As the only novel she wrote, Wuthering Heights won her a position as a great writer in English literature and world literature.

Set in the moorlands of northern England at the end of the 18th century, Wuthering Heights is a story of love, hate, revenge, and social class. The story centers on the dynamics of two generations of the residents of Wuthering Heights and Thrushcross Grange, with Catherine Earnshaw's and Heathcliff's ill-fated love as a guiding force. It expresses criticism of social conventions, particularly those surrounding gender and social class.

Wuthering Heights is unique in its literary style. It is written as a series of diary entries by Lockwood, who writes down what he learns from Nelly Dean, former housekeeper of the Wuthering Heights. But within the main narration, there are also narratives voiced by other characters.

Wuthering Heights has an important influence on English literature and is considered one of the greatest love stories in fiction.

I remember reading an article entitled "The effect of nature as positive distractibility on the healing process of patients with cancer in therapeutic settings." Findings of the study indicate that admitted patients viewing natural scenery had less anxiety and pain than admitted patients viewing no natural scenery. I think this article points to the commodity aspect of nature. My own experience also shows that nature has a healing effect. During the summer vacation after finishing senior two, I felt anxious to the extent that I couldn't focus on my studies. Realizing my problem, my parents decided to do something. My father booked a 10-day tour and we went to Lijiang, Dali, Kunming and other places in Yunnan. The beautiful natural scenery, the smell of flowers, plants and grass, the fresh air, etc. not only satisfied my senses, but also my soul. I came back home happy and relaxed.

随着城市化进程的快速推进，越来越多的人住到了城市，被困在一座座钢筋大厦里。许多人只关注城市生活的便利与繁华，但是当我看到摩天大楼上空的蓝天时，我只想独处一方，远离喧嚣，回归自然，去寻找自然之美。

相较于城市，乡村与自然更亲近。在那里，植物自由生长。因此在乡村，你会更容易感受到自然神奇的生命力。

自然对城市的影响是巨大的。例如，植物可以净化空气，调节大气。湖泊可以净化水，调节当地气候。

只要我们能把更多的自然元素融入城市，我们必定能够获得自然更多的馈赠，我们的生活品质也无疑会提高。
